correctness.rationale: Symmetry averaging is valid for the convex spectral norm ||P−Π|| of symmetric stochastic matrices and preserves both pointwise edge floors, proving global reduction to common rim/rung weights. Fourier spectrum on C_m square K2 (Cartesian product) yields three sharp endpoint inequalities 1−ar, 1−2v, br+2v−1 for SLEM. Five resulting lower bounds are also sufficient using r=max(tau,(1−t)/a), v=max(eta,(1−t)/2); analytic a+b>4 proves feasibility for every m≥4 and every 2tau+eta≤1. Odd m needs all five facets, even m the 4tau−1 facet is redundant. An independent SciPy linear program solved 500 parameter instances for m=4..13, matching the claimed optimum to 4.44e−16; this supports but does not replace the analytic all-size proof.
residual_risks: Independent LP uses floating point for corroboration, not certified infinite feasibility; analytic inequalities supply the proof.

value.rationale: The circular ladder is a canonical 3-regular Cartesian-product network, and mandatory traffic through rim and rung edges is a natural constrained mixing design. The solved global optimum is an exact, all-size two-parameter five-facet frontier with constructive optimizer and parity-dependent redundancy, illustrating nontrivial spectral/stochastic constraint interactions. It goes beyond a generic SDP restatement or a numerical small graph case.
residual_risks: No uniqueness claimed for all nonsymmetrized optimizers and no direct TV mixing-time claim.

limitations: Restricted to symmetric stochastic matrices and uniform stationary distribution on C_m × K2; no arbitrary directed or nonuniform extension.
